title: A nested operation evaluates its inner operand before the outer operation
summary: A compositional model assigns an inside-out evaluation order to nested operation records, so the outer result consumes the completed inner result rather than the original input.

design.unit: a record with visibly nested inner and outer operation shells and a carried operand
design.contrast: inner-first composition versus flat left-to-right sequencing
design.prediction: Where both shells are present, the outer operation should take the inner result as its operand; changing the inner operand should alter the outer input while leaving an untouched external operand unchanged.
design.countermodel: The same surface pattern could arise from a context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial packaging without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: The outer operation consistently targets the original operand while the inner result is an independent side product, under a fixed nested construction.
design.principal_risk: Nested shell boundaries and operation/result meanings are not independently bound. Near composition and continuation families, but the falsifier is operand routing inside a nested unit.
